attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter. The quoted phrase 'AI bets have paid off' is something he attributes to others, and he is describing it, not endorsing it.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'for the most part', the credit-for-revenue framing and 'barely started to come online'. It is correctly classed as an observation about the present state.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: 'everyone' is treated as emphasis, and 'barely started' means only a small fraction of the AI investment is operational. The Q2 2026 period is a reasonable latest-reported quarter. Requiring representative coverage plus a commissioning denominator is demanding but fair.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own statement that new in-quarter Azure capacity was quickly monetized. It does not give the operational share of the four companies' cumulative AI investment.
One contemporaneous article showing investors reacting differently from company to company. A single piece cannot show whether positive attribution predominated, and it has no deployment data.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative coverage sample and no matched deployment denominator. Microsoft's disclosure that capacity was monetized cuts mildly against the claim but is a company statement and covers one firm only. MoneyWeek shows mixed sentiment but cannot establish whether coverage predominantly credited AI. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'entirely', 'any AI chip', the four or five customers and Huang's statements. It is correctly classed as an exclusive causal claim.

contract.note: Reading 'manufactured' as speculative accumulation plus misleading claims, rather than genuine downstream use, is ordinary. Treating 'entirely' as exclusive causation matches the words. The contract rightly says concentrated buying alone does not prove the demand is artificial.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure of more than 30 million paid Copilot seats. It suggests some downstream demand but does not link that demand to particular chip purchases, so it cannot meet the contradiction condition on its own.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no causal breakdown of chip purchases, no record tracing them to downstream use, and no check of Huang's statements. Paid Copilot adoption is relevant counter-context, but it is a company disclosure and is not tied to chip purchasing. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own concluding prediction in his newsletter.

semantics.note: This is a forecast with no deadline ('ultimately', 'eventual'). The proposition keeps 'I think', the range of losses from embarrassment to destruction, and the claim that more spending makes the collapse worse.

contract.note: Declining to adjudicate is fair. 'Loses' includes embarrassment, the investor population is undefined, there is no endpoint, and 'more gruesome' has no counterfactual. Any narrower financial test would add a meaning the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: A Reuters report from 14 October 2026 of a selloff in AI infrastructure stocks and record default-insurance costs. A short-term market setback cannot show ultimate losses for everybody.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline and no measurable definition of 'loses' (which includes embarrassment), of 'everybody', or of the collapse being 'more gruesome'. No fair binary test exists, so it is not scored. The October 2026 selloff is context only.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The Microsoft part is stated firmly ('very clear'). The industry-wide part is an inference he says he believes. The proposition preserves both parts and the difference in firmness between them.

contract.note: Reading 'silly buggers' as materially blurring operational AI capacity with broader capacity, without requiring proof of deliberate deception, is a fair, ordinary reading. The July to September 2026 window is chosen by the evaluator but reasonable. Marking the outcome as known at freeze is odd, since the packet does not settle it.

evidence.note: Nadella calls the one gigawatt added 'overall capacity' and does not define its power basis. This is mild contrary context: it does not show Microsoft presenting all of it as AI capacity, but it does not prove the definitions are clear either.
CoreWeave's definition of 'active power', given in March 2026. It predates the target period and does not cover the later 850MW claim.

reviews.rationale: The September report with the 12GW and 2GW figures could not be read. There is no reconciliation of what Microsoft's capacity figures include, and no industry-wide comparison. Microsoft's 'overall capacity' wording and CoreWeave's earlier definition are context only. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
